Title: Luciferi Calaritani Opuscula, recensuit et commentario critico instruxit Guilelmus Hartel (Corpus Scriptorum Ecclesiasticorum Latinorum vol. XIV)
Creator: Lucifer of Cagliari (d. c. 370); Wilhelm von Hartel (ed.)
Publisher: Vindobonae: apud C. Geroldi filium bibliopolam Academiae
Publication Date: 1886 (MDCCCLXXXVI on the title pages, file lines 39 and 56)
Rights: Public Domain (pd-us-by-date: published 1886); the archive.org record tags it NOT_IN_COPYRIGHT
Language: lat (Latin; cleanly recovered in the text, with Hartel's apparatus; no Greek in the volume)
Source: archive.org item corpusscriptorum14luciuoft (Robarts Library, University of Toronto; catalogue volume 14), full text at https://archive.org/download/corpusscriptorum14luciuoft/corpusscriptorum14luciuoft_djvu.txt. Fetched directly 2026-10-17 by the Shared-Events source-research thread (Era 2 worker A); the byte count of the downloaded file (1,866,040) equals the size archive.org lists for the djvu.txt. A second scan of the same edition, archive.org item lucifericalarita14luci, was checked the same day and not vendored (smaller, more broken OCR).
Provenance note: Extracted unaltered: the item's own djvu.txt is reproduced whole after this header; nothing was stripped, normalized or corrected. Rights basis: an 1886 Vienna printing is out of US copyright under this project's pd-us-by-date rule; the host's NOT_IN_COPYRIGHT tag is supporting evidence.
Content note: The pamphlets Lucifer wrote in exile (355-361) against Constantius II after the synod of Milan (355) condemned Athanasius in his absence and exiled the bishops who refused to sign: De non conueniendo cum haereticis (file line 2628), De regibus apostaticis (file line 4039), De sancto Athanasio books I and II (file lines 5463 and 9342; the first also titled Quia absentem nemo debet iudicare nec damnare, file line 5491), De non parcendo in Deum delinquentibus (file line 12300) and Moriendum esse pro Dei Filio (file line 15818), with Liberius's letters to Lucifer in exile (file line 17490) and a mention of the Ariminum council (file line 1218). The hard-line Western Nicene voice that refused the compromises of 355-360 and later broke with the bishops who had signed at Ariminum (the 'Luciferian' schism Jerome's Dialogue answers); a primary dissenting voice, not a narrative of the councils.
